rect.title: Create a Cloudflare R2 bucket and access key. Done 2026-10-17: bucket onlycars-dev, credentials in the API project's user-secrets (R2:AccountId, R2:AccessKeyId, R2:SecretAccessKey, R2:BucketName).

(Agreed by the owner, 2026-10-17.) Review the delegated decisions in docs/decisions.md, especially the 12 starter task intervals, the task status rules (when a task counts as "Due soon" or "Overdue"), the Reset and Undo rules (a one-tap reset counts as DIY; Undo only for the latest reset of a task), the settings rules (changing the currency does not convert old amounts; only ILS, USD, EUR and GBP), the km/miles rules (converted template intervals such as 6,214 mi rather than round mile values; the unit is not asked at sign-up; the Hebrew label "קילומטראז׳" kept in miles), the service history rules (undone records are hidden; an old service never moves a task's last done backwards; Undo works on any record, in any order; a corrected later-dated service at a lower odometer moves last done to that lower reading), the line item rules (the total becomes the sum of the items whenever there are items), the search rules (a separate Service history page for all cars, read-only, with edit and delete staying on the car page; the search doesn't look in task names), and the edit rules for MVP3-D (changing a service's date, odometer or tasks moves the car's odometer and the tasks' last done; a service can't be moved to another car), two readings on the same day ordered by when they were saved (ordering by value was tried and reverted), and the dashboard rules (home page /; this month's spend includes archived cars so it matches the Service history page; one-tap Mark done without cost or notes; a task moves down its card after Mark done because cards follow urgency), the checklist rules (your own checklists only, no ready-made ones for now; a checklist can be "manual only" with no schedule, even though the spec's data rules ask for an interval; units on number items are free text and not converted; a checklist is due soon at 10% of its interval left, with no setting; Not OK and a number outside its range are flagged automatically; runs can be deleted but not edited; due checklists are not counted in the dashboard's Overdue and Due soon numbers; actions hidden on archived cars and on turned-off checklists; a 30-day schedule reads "Every 1 month"), and the to-do rules for MVP5-C (a flagged checklist item becomes a to-do you create with one tap, not automatically and not a maintenance task, because a maintenance task can't say "fix this now"), and the LOW-3 choices (dates before 1900 rejected; a number sent instead of a name for a choice field is rejected; the old browser QA scripts deleted), and the tire rules for MVP5-D (tire sets on a new Tires page; mounting a set on a car that has one is a swap; mounting and unmounting don't add an odometer reading; a full purchase date rather than a year; deleting a set deletes its history), and the MVP5-E tire check rules (pressure in bar only, also for miles users; no low-tread warning yet; one check per set per day; a rotation is a dated note and does not reset a maintenance task; a check is stored as one dated header with a row per wheel, slightly different from the spec's data model), and the Hebrew form of address (singular, לך and שלך, everywhere).
Tell us when the ui-tester (browser QA) may run again. Restarted by the owner, 2026-10-17; a catch-up pass covers the tickets shipped without it.

(Report rules, the Hebrew TCO term and the export plan agreed by the owner, 2026-10-17.) When you next use Reports, open one exported CSV in Excel and try "Print or save as PDF" once; no agent can check either.

Decide whether to clear the test users from your local database. scripts/cleanup-test-users.sql deletes only accounts with machine-generated test emails (from the browser tests, test scripts and agents, such as ui-...@onlycars.test and qa+...@example.com; 1,056 of the 1,153 accounts when counted, more since) and all their data. It never matches your own accounts. It also covers the report test users (rpt1-…, ui-rpt-…, probe-rpt-…), added in LOW-5; and the photo and receipt test users (file1-…, be-file1-fix…, file2-…, file3-…), added in FILE-2 and FILE-3. LOW-6 added the browser-QA and other agent accounts (qa3-…, qa-…, shot-…, mvp…, sec… and more); only your own accounts and two short demo-like accounts (demo+…, ui+… at onlycars.test) are left out. Run the dry run first; it lists the accounts and changes nothing: sqlcmd -S "(localdb)\MSSQLLocalDB" -d OnlyCars -E -b -v DryRun=1 -i scripts/cleanup-test-users.sql (the database is OnlyCars, from src/OnlyCars.Api/appsettings.json). -v DryRun=0 deletes. LOW-6 also added a guard: the script stops if any account it would delete is outside the test domains, so a gmail account can never be deleted. NOT-1 and ACC-1 left new test users not1-…, qa-not1-…, acc1-… and qa-acc1-…; rules for not1-… and acc1-… are added in LOW-8. LOW-6 ran the dry run only (2026-10-18: 1,713 of the 1,718 accounts listed, none of yours); nothing has been deleted. LOW-9 removed six real domains (such as x.com and test.com) from the script, so 22 test users on those domains are no longer matched; delete them by hand if you want them gone. Since LOW-11 the script runs only on the database OnlyCars (and its own test copies); on any other database it stops and deletes nothing.

Turn on the daily reminder email (done 2026-11-03: Gmail app password, Render settings and the cron-job.org job; the first email arrived) (NOT-2; you chose Gmail, 2026-11-02; nothing is sent until this is done). (1) Create a new Gmail account for the site, e.g. onlycars.reminders@gmail.com. (2) In that account: Google Account, Security, turn on 2-Step Verification (Gmail requires it for app passwords). (3) Then go to myaccount.google.com/apppasswords, create an app password named OnlyCars, and copy the 16 letters (shown once; spaces don't matter). (4) In Render, your service, Environment, add: Email__SmtpUser = the new Gmail address; Email__SmtpPassword = the app password; Email__SiteUrl = https://onlycars-ev28.onrender.com; Email__JobKey = a long random string (keep it private). Save; Render restarts the site. (5) Because the free plan sleeps when nobody uses the site, set up a free daily cron at cron-job.org: every day at 08:00, time zone Asia/Jerusalem, method POST, URL https://onlycars-ev28.onrender.com/api/jobs/daily-digest, header X-Job-Key = the same random string. The first call may time out while the site wakes; the site then sends anyway, because it is past 08:00. Each user gets at most one email a day, only when something needs attention, and can turn it off in Settings. (Resend still works instead: Email__ResendApiKey and Email__From, which needs a domain of your own to reach anyone but you.)

Check the R2 access key's permissions in the Cloudflare dashboard (R2, Manage API tokens): it should allow only "Object Read & Write" on the one bucket onlycars-dev, not all buckets and not admin. The photo links show the key's id (never the secret), and security accepted that only with this narrow scope. Production will get its own bucket and key.

(Agreed by the owner, 2026-10-24.) Reminder choices made for you in NOT-1, which you may change: (1) the driving license is recorded on a car, like insurance; it could live on your account instead; (2) document costs (insurance, fees) show on the document only and don't count in Reports or the total cost of ownership; (3) reminders come from each task's Due soon percent, with no extra "remind me N km before" setting; (4) the English counts on the dashboard say "tasks" and count tasks only, not checklists or documents.

(Agreed by the owner, 2026-10-24.) For ACC-1 (data export), a choice made for you: the file lists your receipts and photos by name but does not include the files themselves. Say if you want them bundled in a ZIP.

(Agreed by the owner, 2026-10-24.) Limits chosen for you in ACC-1, which you may change: up to 50 cars per account (archived ones count), 2,000 service records and 5,000 odometer readings per car. They keep one account (and its export) from growing without end; existing data is never touched.

(Agreed by the owner, 2026-10-24.) For ACC-2 (delete your account), a choice made for you: deleting is immediate and permanent after you type your password, with no 30-day grace period. Say if you want a grace period.

Try Scan once on your Android phone: open a service on a car, tap Scan, photograph a real receipt, drag the corners onto it, type a name, Save, and open the PDF. Do it once more on a car document (Documents, Scan). Also press the phone's Back button while the scanner is open: it should close the scanner (asking first if you have pages). No agent has a real phone camera.
Optional: do you want an "Install app" button inside OnlyCars? For now there is none; Chrome's own menu (Install OnlyCars) does it. Default: no button.

If you want a fuel log (optional, spec 11), answer two questions: (1) do you log only full tanks, or partial fills too? (2) should consumption show as L/100 km, km/L or mpg, or follow your km/miles setting? It won't start until you answer.

When you want, remove leftover storage files that belong to deleted accounts (no agent will run this against your bucket). In src/OnlyCars.Api, first run dotnet run --launch-profile http -- sweep-orphans, which only lists what it would delete. Its first line names the bucket and database it compared: check they are the ones you mean. If the list looks right, run it again with --delete. If most folders in the bucket are leftovers, which is likely because of test accounts, it also needs --force. Don't run it while tests are running.
Create an Azure account and deploy (done: the site runs on Render with the database on Azure SQL).
Turn on "Sign in with Google" (done: the Client ID is set on the live site and you signed in with Google there).

Choose who may use OnlyCars (invite-only since 2026-10-30: nobody can register, and Google sign-in makes no new accounts). To let someone in, in src/OnlyCars.Api run dotnet run --launch-profile http -- add-user friend@gmail.com (several emails at once are fine). The first line names the database it writes to; check it is the one you mean. The person then opens the login page and clicks "Sign in with Google" with that Google account; that first sign-in links the account. While your Google consent screen is in "Testing" mode, also add each person under "Test users" there (up to 100), or Google itself refuses them. To open registration again for everyone, set Auth:OpenRegistration to true (the browser tests run the API that way).

Question: should the Honda (הונדה) have tires? Checked on the live site on 2026-11-04: the Mazda (מאזדה) shows its 4 GOODYEAR DURAPLUS 2 winter tires, fitted 2026-11-03, 920 km on them. The Honda shows no tires. The move to tires per wheel carried over only sets that were on a car; a set that was never mounted stays in the old tables only, and we could not look into the live database to see whether the Honda had one. If the Honda should have tires, tell us which (brand, size, season) and we will bring them back; or add them yourself with Add tires on the Honda's Tires. If it never had any, say so. Until you answer, the old Legacy_ tire tables stay (L222).
Email/password login, and Sign in with Google (live; you signed in with Google on the live site)
Mobile-first and installable as an app (44px tap targets, no sideways scrolling; app icons and an install checked in Chrome, PWA-1)
Light and dark mode (System, Light or Dark in Settings)

Each user's data is private, plus data export and delete-account ("Export my data" in Settings, ACC-1; "Delete my account" in Settings with your password, ACC-2: removes the account, all its data and its files, and signs out other devices)
Hebrew and English, including right-to-left
Receipt image storage with size limits (10 MB per file, 1 GB per account, shared by the car photo, receipts and run photos; the files are deleted with the account, ACC-2)
Offline odometer entry that syncs later (on the dashboard; sent by itself when you are back online, never twice, OFF-1)

Error reporting (owner, 2026-11-03): website and server errors are recorded automatically (what failed, on which screen and browser), so bugs are found and fixed without you having to notice and report them. Needs a free Sentry account from you when we build it.

Scan documents from the phone (owner, 2026-11-03): like CamScanner: photograph a receipt or document, the app finds its edges, straightens and crops it, and makes it look like a clean scanned page (white background, sharp text); several pages can become one PDF. Scan, next to "Add file" on a service and on a car document (SCAN-1 and SCAN-2): camera or a saved image, you drag the 4 corners onto the paper, then Black and white or Color, up to 20 pages saved as one PDF with the name you choose. Missing: the app finding the edges by itself (it needs an 8 MB add-on that would not work offline; ask if you want it). In Black and white a very large solid block (over about 1/8 of the page) still comes out as an outline, and the dots on the i's of very small print can be lost.

Name the scan, and files and Scan on car documents (owner, 2026-11-04): type a file name in the scanner before Save (default scan-YYYY-MM-DD, .pdf added for you); car documents (insurance, inspection, registration, licence) get Add file and Scan like a service, with the same limits (10 MB a file, 10 files, the 1 GB total); their files are in the full export and deleted with the document or the account. SCAN-2a and SCAN-2b, signed off 2026-11-04, not committed yet.

🔨 My files page (owner, 2026-11-03): one place to see every uploaded file (receipts, service files, checklist photos, car photos, document files) with its car and service, run or document, and how much of the 1 GB is used. Next ticket: MYF-1a (server), then MYF-1b (the page).

Full export with files (owner, 2026-11-03, major): "Download everything (ZIP)" in Settings, next to "Export my data": one ZIP with the data file and every stored file (car photos, receipts and service files, checklist run photos), in a folder per car; a file that can't be read is listed in missing-files.txt (EXP-1, signed off 2026-11-04). Car documents have no files of their own yet (SCAN-2 adds them, and the export will include them); their details are in the data file.
Fuel log and consumption tracking (needs your answers first; see "Waiting on the owner")
Issue / to-do list (optional; per car only: open and done to-dos on the car page, and the open count on the dashboard. No list across all cars.)
Shared access (partner or family)
Garage directory
Parts and warranty tracking
Full data import/export
OBD-II / manufacturer API odometer
Step 1: Accounts, cars, odometer. Done (MVP1-A, B and C signed off). Settings signed off: language, theme and currency (SET-1), and km or miles (SET-2). Car photo signed off (FILE-1).
Step 2: Maintenance tasks, templates, Reset. Done (MVP2-A, B and C signed off).

Step 3: Service history with costs Done. MVP3-A, B, C and D signed off (history list, record a past service with parts and labour, edit everything including date, odometer and tasks, delete, filter and search on the Service history page), LOW-1, and FILE-2 (receipt photos and PDFs on each service).

Step 4: Dashboard with due and overdue status MVP4-A signed off (the dashboard on /: overdue and due-soon counts, this month's spend linking to the history, each car's next 3 tasks with Mark done and Undo, quick odometer entry). LOW-2 signed off. Start a checklist signed off with MVP5-B.

Step 5: Checklists, then tires, then reports and notifications MVP5-A, MVP5-B and MVP5-C signed off (your own checklists; attach them to a car with a schedule, run them with flags, run history, Start a checklist on the dashboard; a flagged item becomes a to-do on the car). MVP5-D and MVP5-E signed off (tire sets, mount and swap, km per set, storage notes, pressure and tread checks, rotations). LOW-4 (small fixes) signed off. RPT-1 signed off (the Reports page: costs per car, category, month and year, cost per km, total cost of ownership). RPT-2 signed off (bar charts per month and per category). RPT-3 signed off (export to CSV and PDF). LOW-5 (small fixes) signed off. FILE-3 signed off (photos on checklist runs). LOW-6 (small fixes to files and photos), LOW-7 (small fixes to reports, dashboard and checklists) and LOW-8 (dates that agree around midnight, and small fixes) signed off. Everything above has been checked in a browser. NOT-1 (in-app reminders with documents, snooze and lead days) signed off. NOT-2 (the daily reminder email through Gmail) live since 2026-11-03. TIRE-2 (tires per wheel) live, checked 2026-11-04.
Before going online: SEC-1 (limit login attempts, account lockout, constant-time login). Signed off.
Tire sets: brand, model, size, season, purchase year (a full purchase date), DOT code
Which set is on which car, with mount and unmount dates
Km driven per set, calculated automatically
Pressure log, tread depth log, rotation tracking (pressure in bar only)
Storage notes for the off-season set

Tires per wheel with a top-view car (your request, TIRE-2a and TIRE-2b, live, checked 2026-11-04): each wheel has its own tire with its history, Replace tires for one, a pair or all four creating a "Tires" service record, a drawn car with tappable wheels; your mounted sets became four tires each. (A wrong km or date in Replace can't be corrected yet, L232.)
Checklist templates
Items: checkbox, number or text (numbers with a unit and an allowed range)
Schedule by km, by time, or manual only

Run a checklist: tick items, add notes or photos, flag issues (photos are added to a saved run: "Add photos" right after saving, or from the run in the history; up to 10 per run, JPEG, PNG or WebP, opened in a new tab; deleting the run deletes its photos)
Failed items create a to-do or a maintenance task (a to-do, as decided)
Run history per car
Task name and category
Interval by km, by time, or both (whichever comes first)
Starter template library, fully editable (12 templates; the owner should review their intervals)
Custom tasks per car
Turn a task off without deleting it
Date, odometer, shop or DIY, total cost, notes (one record can cover several tasks)
Line items: part, brand, part number, quantity, unit cost, labour (total is the sum of the items)

Attachments: receipt photos, PDFs, invoices (added to a saved service from its row on the car page, up to 10 files of 10 MB each; opened from the Service history page too; not on the Record a service form; iPhone photos are sent as JPEG, HEIC is refused)
Filter and search by car, task, date or shop (Service history page, all cars, filters kept in the link)
Edit and delete past records (everything on a record, including date, odometer and tasks; the car's odometer and the tasks' last done follow)
Add, edit and archive cars, keeping their history
Fields: nickname, make, model, year, VIN, plate, fuel type, purchase date, photo (one photo per car, on the car page; not on dashboard cards)
Current odometer, with a history of readings, which you can edit and delete
Multiple cars per account (up to 50, archived ones included)
Manual odometer updates with a quick-entry button (on the car page and on each dashboard card)
Auto-log the odometer when a service is recorded (Mark done and the Record a service form)
Average km/day, used to predict due dates
Km/miles unit, and a currency per user (both in Settings; every distance on screen is converted)
Remaining km and days, a progress bar, and status: OK, Due soon, Overdue
Reset / Mark as done (records odometer and date, restarts the countdown, creates a history entry with optional cost and notes)
Undo for accidental resets (right after the reset, and any record from the service history)
Configurable "due soon" threshold (percent, 1 to 50)
Cost per car, per category, per month and per year (Reports page; a service on several categories is split equally)
Cost per km and total cost of ownership (per mile for miles users; TCO is purchase price plus services)
Charts: spending over time, cost by category (bars per month and per category on the Reports page; right to left in Hebrew)
Export to CSV and PDF (a CSV of the service records for the chosen year and car, and a PDF from the browser's print dialog; nobody has opened the CSV in Excel yet)
Email when a task is due soon or overdue (NOT-2: a daily email through Gmail at 08:00 Israel time, on since 2026-11-03, first email received; off switch in Settings; push not built)

Non-mileage reminders: insurance, inspection, registration, license (in the app: documents on each car page, and a Reminders card on the dashboard with due tasks, due checklists and expiring documents; the driving license sits on a car)
Snooze, and a configurable lead time (snooze for 1 day, 1 week or 1 month, with Undo; the days-ahead setting in Settings applies to documents; tasks keep their own Due soon percent)
All cars at a glance, next due items sorted by urgency
Overdue count and monthly spend summary (links to the Service history for the same month)
Quick actions: update odometer, reset a task, start a checklist
